title: Collection of Deposits and Prepayments on Hotel Rate Plans
content:
A rate plan of the Hotel Rate Plans range that requires prepayment takes its prepayment share of the room total at the moment the property confirms, and a plan that does not takes its deposit expressed in room nights instead.

**What a deposit is measured on.** A deposit is measured on the room rate alone, before taxes and before any mandatory facility fee; those are settled at the property unless the plan is prepaid in full. The basis of a deposit is therefore the room rate before taxes and mandatory fees, and nothing else.

**Currency.** A prepaid reservation is charged in the currency the property publishes, and a conversion the guest elects carries the plan's markup.

**Where the card is declined.** Where the property declines the card, the reservation stays merely reserved and is released when the hold lapses; a reservation is never confirmed against an unpaid deposit.

**What becomes of the money.** A deposit already taken is applied against the first night's room charge at check-in and is never treated as a separate payment to be refunded afterwards. Where the guest later cancels, the deposit is the first money the cancellation penalty is withheld from.

*Points of judgement.* A plan whose contracted share of the room total is taken at booking takes that share and no deposit in nights; a plan that takes a deposit in nights takes those nights measured on the room rate alone. Taxes and the mandatory facility fee sit outside the deposit basis on a plan that is not prepaid in full, and are settled at the property.
